title: Polynomial mixing of planar Ising dynamics with plus boundaries
formal:
For every fixed finite inverse temperature \(\beta\in[0,\infty)\), does random-site heat-bath Glauber dynamics for the zero-field nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model on \(V_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}^{2}\), with all exterior boundary spins fixed to \(+1\), mix in time polynomial in \(n\)? Precisely, is it true that
\[\forall\beta\in[0,\infty)\ \exists C_\beta,a_\beta>0\ \forall n\ge1,\qquad t_{\mathrm{mix}}^+(n,\beta,1/4)\le C_\beta(n+1)^{a_\beta}?\]
The mixing time is worst-case over every initial configuration inside the box and counts individual site-update attempts. The constants may depend on the fixed temperature, but not on \(n\). The finite-temperature convention and the update rule are specified below.
why: This question asks whether fixing a coherent boundary phase is enough to make local sampling efficient at every positive temperature. At low temperature, convergence from an opposing interior phase is controlled by the disappearance of large interfaces. A polynomial bound would quantify how boundary information removes the slow phase switching that occurs under other boundary conditions.

progress.text: Lubetzky, Martinelli, Sly and Toninelli publish quasipolynomial mixing for the planar low-temperature Ising model with all-plus boundary conditions.
The second edition of Markov Chains and Mixing Times keeps the polynomial bound as Question 1 and updates its known upper bound to quasipolynomial.

Gheissari and Sly state the polynomial mixing question explicitly and prove a uniform-in-low-temperature quasipolynomial bound as an ingredient for rapid phase ordering from biased starts; the preprint does not claim the worst-state polynomial target.

importance.reason: A long-standing model question about whether boundary phase selection makes local sampling efficient throughout the planar Ising model’s low-temperature regime. It connects geometric interface relaxation with worst-state Markov-chain mixing and remains explicitly open in 2026 primary work.

sentences: Fixing plus spins around a planar Ising box selects a boundary phase while the interior spins evolve randomly.
The question asks whether local heat-bath updates mix in polynomial time at every fixed positive temperature.
The bound must hold from every interior starting configuration, including the all-minus state.
Polynomial constants may depend on temperature but cannot grow with the box size.
The checked 2026 source retains this question while improving quasipolynomial mixing and proving rapid ordering from more favorable initializations.

definitions:
Vertices are adjacent when their lattice distance \(\|u-v\|_1=|u_1-v_1|+|u_2-v_2|\) is one. Let \(E_n\) consist of the unordered adjacent pairs inside \(V_n\), and let \(\partial V_n\) be the vertices outside \(V_n\) adjacent to it. A state is \(\sigma\in\Omega_n=\{-1,+1\}^{V_n}\). Extend it to \(\widetilde\sigma\) by assigning \(+1\) to every vertex of \(\partial V_n\). The Gibbs measure is
\[\pi_{n,\beta}^+(\sigma)=\frac1{Z_{n,\beta}^+}\exp\!\left(\beta\left[\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E_n}\sigma_u\sigma_v+\sum_{\substack{u\in V_n,\ v\in\partial V_n\\\|u-v\|_1=1}}\sigma_u\right]\right),\]
where the normalizing constant is the sum of this weight over \(\Omega_n\). Internal and crossing edges are each counted once and all interaction strengths are one. There is no external field beyond the effect of the fixed boundary spins. A corner vertex has two crossing edges; each contributes to its local field.

At each discrete step choose \(v\in V_n\) uniformly and independently, and replace \(\sigma_v\) by \(+1\) with probability
\[\frac{\exp(\beta h_v(\sigma))}{\exp(\beta h_v(\sigma))+\exp(-\beta h_v(\sigma))},\qquad h_v(\sigma)=\sum_{u:\|u-v\|_1=1}\widetilde\sigma_u,\]
and by \(-1\) otherwise. The other interior spins are unchanged and exterior spins are never updated. An update that retains the old value counts as a step. For every finite \(\beta\), the chain has strictly positive conditional probabilities, is irreducible and aperiodic, and has stationary measure \(\pi_{n,\beta}^+\). Denote its transition matrix by \(P_{n,\beta}^+\).

Total-variation distance between distributions \(\nu,\pi\) on the finite state space is \(\operatorname{TV}(\nu,\pi)=\frac12\sum_{\sigma\in\Omega_n}|\nu(\sigma)-\pi(\sigma)|\). Define
\[t_{\mathrm{mix}}^+(n,\beta,1/4)=\min\{t\in\mathbb N_0:\max_{\sigma\in\Omega_n}\operatorname{TV}((P_{n,\beta}^+)^t(\sigma,\cdot),\pi_{n,\beta}^+)\le1/4\}.\]
The maximum includes the all-minus interior configuration; it is not restricted to typical or mostly-plus starts. The boundary is plus throughout, regardless of the interior initial state.

Inverse temperature is measured in units with interaction strength and Boltzmann constant equal to one. The domain includes \(\beta=0\), the independent-spin infinite-temperature limit, and every positive physical temperature, but not the separate zero-temperature limit \(\beta=\infty\). The quantified statement is pointwise in fixed \(\beta\); it does not demand common constants for temperatures varying with \(n\). In the continuous-time convention with one rate-one clock per interior site, the typical update count per unit time is \(n^2\). This polynomial factor preserves the question of a polynomial mixing bound, but matters when comparing exact exponents. This card studies the exact mathematical chain, not finite-precision implementation of its probabilities.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the displayed all-finite-temperatures polynomial bound or its negation. A positive answer must cover every fixed finite \(\beta\) and every interior initial state with all-plus boundaries. A negative answer must establish at least one fixed finite inverse temperature for which no polynomial in box side length bounds the specified mixing time. Bounds only from biased initializations, only in the zero-temperature limit, or of quasipolynomial size do not meet the target.

context_blocks.text: Question 1 of the source is explicitly two-dimensional: an n by n grid with all-plus boundaries. Its remarks about higher dimensions are related context, not an enlargement of this card’s quantifiers.

The published Lubetzky–Martinelli–Sly–Toninelli bound is \(n^{c(\beta)\log n}\) in the low-temperature regime. It is a substantial improvement over earlier subexponential bounds, but its exponent grows with \(n\), so it is not polynomial.

The May 2026 Gheissari–Sly preprint still identifies polynomial plus-boundary mixing as a long-standing open problem. Its Theorem 4 strengthens control of the temperature dependence in a quasipolynomial bound. Its rapid phase-ordering theorem uses biased initial configurations and a different convergence target, rather than providing the worst-state polynomial mixing bound here.

Zero-temperature interface dynamics and finite-temperature mixing are distinct statements. The new preprint discusses the known zero-temperature polynomial bounds as supporting evidence, while retaining the finite-temperature question. The card fixes finite inverse temperature to avoid treating a non-irreducible limiting chain as the same ergodic model.
